parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A metal rod is accelerated uniformly from rest in a uniform magnetic field as shown in Fig. 7.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The rod has length *l* and the flux density of the magnetic field is *B*.

An electromotive force (e.m.f.) is induced in the rod. The variation with time *t* of the induced e.m.f. *E* is shown in Fig. 7.2.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: Explain how Fig. 7.2 shows that *E* is proportional to the velocity *v* of the rod.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use Faraday’s law to show that the variation of *E* with time *t* is given by

*E* = *B**l**a**t*

where *a* is the acceleration of the rod.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The length of the rod is 0.45 m. The acceleration *a* of the rod is 7.8 m s⁻².

Determine the value of *B*.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: A vertical metal rod moves to the right through a magnetic field directed into the page.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.2
figures.alt: A graph of induced e.m.f. E in mV against time t in seconds, with a straight line rising from the origin to 0.3 mV at 2 s.
